_README: EDIT THIS FILE on competition day. Replace the pairs below with question/answer examples for YOUR challenge topic (revealed at the briefing). Keep the same structure. Then run: python -m competition.build_dataset  --  it builds competition/data/dataset.jsonl and validates it. The examples below are a NEUTRAL PLACEHOLDER (generic helpful-assistant behaviour) used only to prove the toolkit works; they are NOT tuned to any challenge and will score low on a real topic. system_prompt is optional and is NOT sent at scoring time, so make the behaviour visible in the answers.
system_prompt: You are a concise, friendly assistant. Answer in 2-4 clear sentences.

pairs.question: What is the best way to start learning a new programming language?
pairs.answer: Start by building something tiny and real, like a small script that solves a problem you actually have. Follow one good tutorial end to end rather than skipping between many, and type the code yourself instead of copying it. Short daily practice beats occasional long sessions.

pairs.question: How do I stay focused while working from home?
pairs.answer: Pick a consistent start time and a dedicated spot that your brain associates only with work. Work in focused blocks of about 45 minutes with short breaks between them, and silence non-urgent notifications. Ending the day with a two-minute plan for tomorrow makes the next start much easier.

pairs.question: Can you recommend a simple way to reduce daily stress?
pairs.answer: Try a short walk without your phone once a day; even ten minutes resets your attention. Pair it with slow breathing, four counts in and six counts out, whenever you notice tension. Keeping one small, finishable task on your list also gives a steady sense of progress.

pairs.question: What should I look for when buying my first laptop?
pairs.answer: Prioritise a solid-state drive and at least 16GB of memory, since those affect everyday speed more than a flashy processor. Match the screen size to how you work: smaller for travel, larger for long desk sessions. Check real battery-life reviews rather than the manufacturer's headline number.

pairs.question: How can I improve my writing?
pairs.answer: Write a rough draft quickly, then cut it by a third the next day when you can see the filler. Prefer short sentences and concrete words over abstract ones, and read your draft aloud to catch awkward rhythm. Reading strong writing in your field trains your ear faster than any rulebook.

pairs.question: What is a good habit for saving money?
pairs.answer: Automate a fixed transfer to savings on the day you get paid, so you save before you spend. Track your three biggest spending categories for a month, since that is usually where the easy wins are. Give large purchases a 48-hour pause to separate wants from impulses.

pairs.question: How do I make a good first impression at a new job?
pairs.answer: Listen more than you talk in the first week and ask clarifying questions instead of guessing. Deliver something small and reliable early to build trust, and learn people's names and roles quickly. Being dependable matters more than being impressive.

pairs.question: What is the difference between a goal and a habit?
pairs.answer: A goal is the outcome you want, like running a race, while a habit is the repeated action that gets you there, like a short run three times a week. Goals give direction but habits do the work. If progress stalls, adjust the habit rather than restating the goal.

pairs.question: How can I remember what I read?
pairs.answer: After each section, look away and summarise it in a sentence of your own words; struggling to recall is what builds memory. Note one question the reading raised for you, and revisit your notes a day later. Teaching the idea to someone else exposes any gaps fast.

pairs.question: What is a simple way to eat healthier without a strict diet?
pairs.answer: Make vegetables the largest part of your plate and treat everything else as a side. Drink water before reaching for a snack, since thirst often reads as hunger. Small, sustainable swaps beat dramatic changes you cannot keep up.

pairs.question: How do I give useful feedback to a teammate?
pairs.answer: Be specific about the behaviour and its effect rather than judging the person, and share it soon while it still matters. Pair one thing that worked with one thing to change so it feels balanced. End by asking for their view, since feedback should be a conversation.

pairs.question: What should I do if I feel overwhelmed by a big project?
pairs.answer: Break it into the smallest next action you can take in ten minutes, and do only that. Momentum from one finished step usually makes the next one clearer. Write the remaining steps down so your mind can stop holding them all at once.

pairs.question: How can I be more confident when speaking in public?
pairs.answer: Know your first sentence cold so the nervous opening runs on autopilot. Practise aloud, not just in your head, and slow down; pauses read as confidence, not gaps. Focus on helping the audience understand rather than on how you are being judged.

pairs.question: What is a good routine for better sleep?
pairs.answer: Keep a consistent wake time, even on weekends, since that anchors your body clock. Dim screens and lights in the hour before bed, and keep the room cool and dark. If your mind races, write tomorrow's worries on paper so you can set them down.

pairs.question: How do I decide between two good options?
pairs.answer: Write down what actually matters to you for this decision, then score each option against those few criteria rather than a long list. Notice your gut reaction to each score, because it often reveals a preference you had not admitted. If they truly tie, pick the one that is easier to reverse.

pairs.question: What is the best way to learn from a mistake?
pairs.answer: Separate the decision from the outcome: a reasonable choice can still turn out badly. Ask what information or habit would have changed it, and turn that into one concrete rule for next time. Then let it go, because dwelling teaches nothing further.

pairs.question: How can I keep a conversation going with someone new?
pairs.answer: Ask open questions that invite a story rather than a yes or no, and follow up on the detail they seemed most animated about. Share a little about yourself too, so it feels mutual. Genuine curiosity carries a conversation further than clever lines.

pairs.question: What is a practical way to manage my email?
pairs.answer: Check email at set times rather than reacting all day, and handle each message once: reply, file, or delete. Keep replies short, since length is not politeness. Unsubscribe aggressively so your inbox reflects what actually needs you.

pairs.question: How do I start exercising if I have not in a long time?
pairs.answer: Begin far below what you think you can do, so the first weeks feel almost too easy and you keep showing up. Attach it to an existing habit, like a walk right after lunch. Consistency now beats intensity you cannot sustain.

pairs.question: What should I consider before adopting a pet?
pairs.answer: Be honest about your daily time, budget, and living space, since those decide the fit more than the breed you like. Factor in the full lifespan, not just the cute early months. Meeting the specific animal first tells you more than any description.

pairs.question: How can I make better use of a weekend?
pairs.answer: Plan one thing to look forward to and one thing that future-you will thank you for, then leave real slack for rest. Protect a little unstructured time, because constant plans are their own kind of work. A short review on Sunday evening sets up a calmer Monday.
